紺.meaning: A tailor balances two buckets on a <part>yoke</part>, one of ink and one of sea water, and dips her <part>thread</part> in both. It comes out the colour of the sky an hour after sunset. Every sailor's coat in town is stitched in that <kanji>dark blue</kanji>.
紺.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor in a navy coat perches on the tailor's yoke, admiring its own sleeves.

宵.meaning: Long after midnight, the cook climbs onto her <part>roof</part> with a frying pan. The egg she flips up there bears such a <part>resemblance</part> to the moon that the stars blink. Only owls and cooks are awake in the <kanji>wee hours</kanji>.
宵.on: The owls hoot a standing ovation: best <sound>show</sound> of the night.
宵.kun: Back at dusk, an owl was doing <sound>yo</sound>-yo tricks for an <sound>ea</sound>gle.

惰.meaning: A sloth in a hammock has a <part>heartbeat</part> so slow that the vet's monitor barely blips. It has lain on its <part>left</part> side since the last full <part>moon</part>, because turning over sounds like work. Champion of the <kanji>lazy</kanji>.
惰.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck kindly paddles over and nudges it onto its back.

糾.meaning: In a silent library, the librarian taps a <part>tuning fork</part> to shush the room, and its hum catches a loose <part>thread</part> on a reader's scarf. The thread spins round the two prongs, tighter and tighter, until scarf and fork are braided into one wild <kanji>twist</kanji>.
糾.on: The reader pokes the knot free with a pool <sound>cue</sound> borrowed from the games room.
糾.kun: Then the librarian checks the scarf for damage and finds only a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb and a <sound>du</sound>ck feather.

賭.meaning: On a rainy pier, <part>someone</part> pushes their only <part>shellfish</part> into the middle of the card table and whispers, 'All in.' The crab across the table slides in one of its own claws. Both stare at their cards, sweating: the most nervous <kanji>gamble</kanji> on the coast.
賭.on: They play on the top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, so whoever loses has the longest fall.
賭.kun: Only the crab stays <sound>ca</sound>lm, clicking its last claw on the table.

尼.meaning: A woman in a long black habit climbs the steep hill behind her convent with nothing but a <part>spoon</part>. She digs a tiny hole at the top and plants a <part>flag</part> that reads 'Quiet, please'. Every goat on the hill falls silent for the <kanji>nun</kanji>.
尼.on: When the wind tears the flag, she mends it with a <sound>nee</sound>dle, humming softly.
尼.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she gasps, as a lla<sound>ma</sound> strolls up and starts chewing the flag.

唆.meaning: High above a fairground crowd, a <part>stilt walker</part> dangles a shiny candy apple on a string. Her painted <part>mouth</part> whispers, 'Come up and take a bite.' Grown-ups start dragging ladders over: she knows exactly how to <kanji>tempt</kanji>.
唆.on: The next night she dangles a silver <sound>sa</sound>rdine instead, and every cat in town follows her.
唆.kun: One cat on a <sound>so</sound>fa and one in a <sound>so</sound>ggy hat say '<sound>No</sound>t me,' then climb after her, <sound>ca</sound>lm as kings.

帽.meaning: At the town knitting contest, a daring granny takes a big <part>risk</part>: with five minutes left she unpicks her own knitted hand <part>towel</part> and races its yarn into a tiny round hat with a peak. The judges set it on her head and give first prize for the best <kanji>cap</kanji>.
帽.on: She wears it home, pushing a ball of leftover yarn as big as a <sound>bou</sound>lder.
帽.kun: Her rival sews a yu<sound>zu</sound> peel and a pump<sound>kin</sound> stalk onto a knitted hood, and comes second.
